issues.legal_issue: Pending objections to an execution sale do not bar a separate application to set aside the sale when the objections raise grounds beyond a challenge to the sale for irregularity or fraud.
material_facts: A decree-holder obtained a money decree, and the judgment-debtors’ property was sold at an execution auction.
The judgment-debtors filed objections concerning the execution and also filed a separate application to set aside the sale after depositing the required amounts.
Some grounds in the objections were not covered by the grounds for challenging a sale under Order XXI, Rule 90.
The lower courts treated the objections as an application under Order XXI, Rule 90 and rejected the separate application as barred.
issues.conclusion: The objections could not be treated as an application under Order XXI, Rule 90, so the bar in Order XXI, Rule 89(2) did not apply merely because those objections were pending.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure, questions between the parties relating to execution may be raised before the executing court. Order XXI, Rule 90 concerns challenges to an execution sale on grounds within that rule, while Rule 89(2) imposes a bar in the circumstances specified there. Objections raising grounds beyond Rule 90 cannot be treated as an application under that rule merely because they concern the execution sale. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.execution_sale_objection_proceeding: The case concerns objections arising from a sale of property in execution of a decree.
predicates.separate_sale_setting_aside_application_: The judgment-debtor filed a separate application to set aside the sale while execution objections remained pending.
predicates.objections_raise_grounds_beyond_sale_irr: The objections include grounds that are not grounds for challenging the sale for irregularity or fraud.

issues.definition: When a separate application to set aside an execution sale is filed while objections containing grounds beyond a sale-irregularity challenge are pending, those objections do not bar the separate application.

issues.legal_issue: Setting aside an execution sale may be conditioned on equitable compensation to the auction-purchaser when the purchaser’s money has remained blocked for a substantial period.
material_facts: The judgment-debtors sought to set aside the execution sale, and the Court concluded that the pending objections did not bar their separate application.
The auction-purchaser’s money had remained blocked for a substantial number of years and was probably more than the amount required by the decree.

The Court directed that the sale be set aside upon payment to the auction-purchaser of the deposited amount with interest, while crediting the judgment-debtors for the amount deposited in court and any interest earned on it.
The Court provided that the appeal would be dismissed if the required payment was not made within the specified time.
issues.conclusion: The sale was to be set aside only if the judgment-debtors paid the auction-purchaser equitable compensation, including interest on the blocked money, with credit for the court deposit and any interest earned on it; otherwise, the appeal would stand dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied equitable fairness in fashioning relief: setting aside the sale without relief for an auction-purchaser whose money had remained blocked for a substantial period would be unfair. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this equitable condition.

predicates.execution_sale_appeal: The case is an appeal concerning a sale conducted in execution of a decree.
predicates.sale_setting_aside_sought: The judgment-debtor seeks to have the execution sale set aside.
predicates.auction_purchaser_funds_blocked_for_subs: The auction-purchaser’s money has remained unavailable to the purchaser for a substantial period.

issues.definition: When an appeal seeks to set aside an execution sale and the auction-purchaser’s funds have been blocked for a substantial time, setting aside the sale is conditioned on equitable compensation to the purchaser.
